title: Adaptive Capacity Adjudicator: region & tier arbitration with variant safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an Adaptive Capacity Adjudicator (ACA) that mediates request routing between Dedicated pools and Hosted endpoints across regions and tiers, while preserving model-variant safety nets. The ACA's goals are: 1) prevent noisy tenants or bursty workloads from starving other tenants in regional Dedicated capacity, 2) enable predictable latency SLOs by reserving short-duration tokens for high-priority requests, 3) allow controlled spill to Hosted with configurable degradation budgets, and 4) maintain warm variant pools to avoid cold-start quality regressions when demoting/preferring fallback variants.
acceptance_criteria: ACA enforces per-tenant soft caps in Dedicated pools without increasing p95 latency > 10% for reserved tier requests
Requests over soft cap are admitted probabilistically with documented fairness heuristic and observable admission rate per tenant
When Dedicated capacity is unavailable, ACA triggers Hosted spillover with per-region rate limits and auto-demote to pre-warmed fallback variants
Circuit-breaker hysteresis prevents flip-flopping: once spilled, tenant waits configured cool-down before reattempting Dedicated allocation
End-to-end tests cover region selection, tier arbitration, and variant swap with no regressions in acceptance harness
design_decisions: Use a lightweight sliding reservation ledger per region/tier (capacity tokens) to represent short-duration commitments instead of long reservations
Admission policy is probabilistic above the soft cap to provide fairness under sustained bursts and to avoid hard rejects
Model variant warm pools are maintained in Dedicated and Hosted with small kept-alive KV caches; fallback variants are kept at lower concurrency but preloaded to avoid cold-run quality dips
Cost-awareness: ACA exposes expected per-token cost delta when spilling to Hosted to inform bitrate-sensitive routes
API-level opt-in flags for tenants: prefer_dedicated, allow_hosted_spill, fallback_variant_preference
implementation_notes: Server-side component: aca-scheduler (Go) running in control plane per region, communicates via gRPC to capacity-proxy and routing service
State: in-memory sliding window ledger persisted to leader-backed Redis for immediate recovery; ledger entries expire after token duration
Admission algorithm: compute tenant_score = baseline_priority * (1 - usage_ratio) + burst_boost; admission probability = sigmoid(k*(threshold - tenant_score))
Fallback variant protocol: send warmup call "variant:prefetch" to Dedicated node and Hosted replica; wait for warmup ACK before demotion
Feature flag rollout: aca.opt_in gating plus kill-switch for automated global revert
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: probabilistic admission could starve low-volume tenants under extreme bursts -> mitigation: min-guarantee tokens per tenant class
Risk: warm pool memory costs increase GPU footprint -> mitigation: LRU eviction on variant cache and adaptive keepalive based on recent traffic
Risk: cross-region coordination latency -> mitigation: local-region ACA decision by default, with global advisory for edge cases
Risk: metadata mismatch between control plane and runtime -> mitigation: add reconciliation job and strong telemetry on ledger drift
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy aca-scheduler to us-west-2 with 5% of tenants in soft-cap enforcement mode
Phase 2 (expanded): enable probabilistic admission + hosted spill to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for non-enterprise tenants; monitor fairness metrics
Phase 3 (default): open opt-in to all tenants and enable variant warm pools for top-100 tenants by traffic; enable cost-exposure headers
Rollback criteria: p95 increase > 15% for reserved-tier requests or Hosted cost increase > 30% vs baseline for >1h
telemetry_and_alerts: Per-tenant admission-rate (Dedicated admit / total requests) stratified by tier and region
Variant-warmup-time histogram and cold-run failure rate
Dedicated-to-Hosted spill volume and per-token cost delta metric
SLO breaches for reserved-tier p95 latency: alert if p95 rises above configured threshold for 5m
Ledger drift alarm: mismatch between control plane tokens and runtime observed usage > 5%
